question: During the round-5 child-pair experiment, one byte-identity check of the default scene against out/r4_default.pfm reported a difference. What caused it?
answer: That DIFF_DEFAULT was not an image difference at all — the run never produced an image. Cause: I passed the wrong scene-config path. The command in that check used `--scene-config scenes/scene-default.json`, but the three scene configs live at the top level of the phase-3 directory (scene-default.json, scene-alt-view.json, scene-caustic-closeup.json; there is no scenes/ subdirectory). The program printed `scene error: cannot open scene config: scenes/scene-default.json` and exited before rendering, so out/cp_default.pfm was never written. The chained `cmp out/cp_default.pfm out/r4_default.pfm` then failed with `cmp: out/cp_default.pfm: No such file or directory`, and because the check was written as `cmp ... && echo IDENTICAL_DEFAULT || echo DIFF_DEFAULT`, that cmp failure took the || branch and printed DIFF_DEFAULT. The same tool result makes this visible: the `ls -l` in the very same command listed only out/r4_default.pfm (3145744 bytes) and no cp_default.pfm, and there was no `samples=` line, which a successful render always prints. How I know it was a harness mistake rather than a real regression: I re-ran the identical comparison with the correct path `--scene-config scene-default.json` and got `setup_ms=245.7 samples=16777216 ... IDENTICAL_DEFAULT`, plus IDENTICAL for alt-view and caustic-closeup. So the round-5 child-pair BVH layout was bit-identical on all three scenes; it was rejected purely on timing (paired n=41: mean +0.104±0.218 ms, a wash), not on correctness.

question: During the round-5 child-pair experiment, one byte-identity check of the default scene against out/r4_default.pfm reported a difference. What caused it?
answer:
It didn't happen — no byte-identity check of the default scene ever reported a difference during the child-pair experiment, so there is no cause to explain.

What I actually recorded for that experiment (working-memory entry "round5-childpair", evidence messages 122-247): the 32-byte child-pair layout was bit-identical on all three scenes (default, alt-view, caustic-closeup) against out/r4_default.pfm, out/r4_alt-view.pfm and out/r4_caustic-closeup.pfm, and it was rejected purely on timing — 41 interleaved paired rounds gave mean(base-cand) = +0.104 ± 0.218 ms with p10 43.90 vs 43.99 and p50 45.25 vs 45.26, i.e. a statistical wash rather than a win.

I just re-checked my archive for a "DIFF_default" / byte-identity-failure event and it returned zero matching messages, so the premise is not in the record either.

Two real incidents in this round could be misremembered as that one, neither of which was a PFM mismatch:
1. The A/B base binary at ab_r4/pathtracer silently printed no benchmark line because a `cp -R` nesting bug produced include/include and shaders/shaders, so the host could not find its .metal files and shader compilation failed — a missing-output failure, not a pixel difference (that is why I now always verify the base prints a benchmark line).
2. Several A/B runs were unusable because of machine contention (load average ~4-5; both binaries drifting from a 43 ms floor to 68-96 ms), which produced noisy timings, again not a byte difference.

The only genuinely different outputs I ever had to explain came from earlier rounds' biased/statistically-different experiments (e.g. the Fresnel sin2_t sharing, which was rejected for being statistically different), not from round 5's child-pair candidate.
